full.description: This image is a gross pathology photograph showing lung tissue. The specimen exhibits dark pigmented areas along with caseous necrosis and calcified granulomatous lesions, particularly near the hilar regions. These characteristic findings are indicative of chronic granulomatous inflammation, most commonly associated with tuberculosis or a similar fungal infection. The cut surface reveals both parenchymal involvement and affected lymph nodes.

random.description: This image is a gross specimen showing a frontal section through lung and mediastinal tissue. It displays grossly enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes containing necrotic areas and anthracotic pigment. The pulmonary parenchyma and surrounding structures are visible on both sides of the section. These findings are characteristic of metastatic carcinoma involving the mediastinal lymph nodes or small cell carcinoma of the lung.
